+# ===========================================================================
+# SELF-HOSTING — COMPOSITION rung: lex → parse → Core → forms, in one Rian module
+# ===========================================================================
+# Goal (ADR-0063 Step 3): the FIRST genuine composition. The per-stage ports
+# (selfhost_lexer/parse/core/beam) are each verified in ISOLATION — diffed against
+# the Elixir reference via projection glue, with no port feeding the next. This
+# module instead wires four stages DIRECTLY, in Rian, over SHARED data types:
+#
+#     lex(String) -> Vec(Tok)            (stage 1, frontend)
+#     parse(Vec(Tok)) -> Surface         (stage 2, precedence climbing)
+#     lower(Surface) -> Core             (stage 3, surface→Core)
+#     forms(Core) -> ErlForm             (stage 4, BEAM abstract forms)
+#
+# `compile(s) = forms(lower(parse(lex(s))))` — each stage hands its output to the
+# next with NO Elixir glue between them. `ErlForm` IS Erlang's abstract-form
+# grammar (`{:integer,_,N}` / `{:var,_,V}` / `{:op,_,Op,L,R}`), so the result feeds
+# `:compile.forms` directly. The only host FFI is `String.to_atom` (Rian can't
+# spell the operator/variable atoms `:+`/`:A`), counted in @selfhost_ffi.
+#
+# `test/rian/compose_fixpoint_test.exs` compiles this composed output and RUNS it,
+# asserting it behaves identically to the full Elixir toolchain (`Rian.Beam`).
+# Scope: the arithmetic expression subset (identifiers, integers, `+ - *`, parens)
+# — small, but REAL Rian source, not a toy language. Widening the subset is the
+# next rung; closing the loop (Stage 3, v1==v2) is the terminus.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+mod SelfhostCompose do
+  # ── shared pipeline types (the seams that let the stages connect) ──
+  type Tok := TNum(String) | TId(String) | TOp(String) | TLP | TRP
+  type Surface := SNum(String) | SId(String) | SBin(String, Surface, Surface)
+  type Core := CNum(String) | CId(String) | CBin(String, Core, Core)
+
+  # ErlForm IS the Erlang abstract-form grammar: Integer -> {:integer, L, N},
+  # Var -> {:var, L, Atom}, Op -> {:op, L, Op, L, R}. Lowers to terms :compile.forms
+  # consumes directly.
+  type ErlForm := Integer(Int53, Int53)
+                | Var(Int53, Symbol)
+                | Op(Int53, Symbol, ErlForm, ErlForm)
+
+  # ── the composed entry point: source -> Erlang abstract form ──
+  pub def compile(s String) ErlForm := forms(lower(parse(lex(s))))
+
+  # ── stage 1: lex (String -> tokens) ──
+  pub def lex(s String) Vec(Tok) := lex_chars(Prim.str_chars(s))
+
+  def lex_chars(Vec(Int53)) Vec(Tok)
+  def lex_chars([]) := []
+  def lex_chars([c | rest])
+    if c == 32 do
+      lex_chars(rest)
+    else
+      classify(c, rest)
+    end
+  end
+
+  # `rest` is the tail AFTER `c`; re-attach `c` to lex the token it starts.
+  def classify(c Int53, rest Vec(Int53)) Vec(Tok)
+  def classify(c, rest)
+    if is_digit(c) do
+      take_num([c | rest], [])
+    else
+      lex_alpha_or_op(c, rest)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def lex_alpha_or_op(c Int53, rest Vec(Int53)) Vec(Tok)
+  def lex_alpha_or_op(c, rest)
+    if is_alpha(c) do
+      take_id([c | rest], [])
+    else
+      take_op([c | rest])
+    end
+  end
+
+  def take_num(Vec(Int53), Vec(Int53)) Vec(Tok)
+  def take_num([], acc) := [TNum(text(acc))]
+  def take_num([c | rest], acc)
+    if is_digit(c) do
+      take_num(rest, [c | acc])
+    else
+      [TNum(text(acc)) | lex_chars([c | rest])]
+    end
+  end
+
+  def take_id(Vec(Int53), Vec(Int53)) Vec(Tok)
+  def take_id([], acc) := [TId(text(acc))]
+  def take_id([c | rest], acc)
+    if is_alnum(c) do
+      take_id(rest, [c | acc])
+    else
+      [TId(text(acc)) | lex_chars([c | rest])]
+    end
+  end
+
+  def take_op(Vec(Int53)) Vec(Tok)
+  def take_op([40 | rest]) := [TLP | lex_chars(rest)]
+  def take_op([41 | rest]) := [TRP | lex_chars(rest)]
+  def take_op([c | rest]) := [TOp(Prim.str_from_chars([c])) | lex_chars(rest)]
+
+  # accumulated codes are reversed (prepended) — reverse, then build the string.
+  def text(acc Vec(Int53)) String := Prim.str_from_chars(rev_codes(acc, []))
+
+  def rev_codes(Vec(Int53), Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53)
+  def rev_codes([], out) := out
+  def rev_codes([c | rest], out) := rev_codes(rest, [c | out])
+
+  def is_digit(c Int53) Bool := c >= 48 and c <= 57
+  def is_alpha(c Int53) Bool := (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or c == 95
+  def is_alnum(c Int53) Bool := is_alpha(c) or is_digit(c)
+
+  # ── stage 2: parse (tokens -> Surface, precedence climbing) ──
+  type PR := PR(Surface, Vec(Tok))
+
+  pub def parse(ts Vec(Tok)) Surface
+  pub def parse(ts)
+    case parse_bp(0, ts) do
+      PR(e, _) -> e
+    end
+  end
+
+  def parse_bp(min_bp Int53, ts Vec(Tok)) PR
+  def parse_bp(min_bp, ts)
+    case primary(ts) do
+      PR(lhs, rest) -> climb(min_bp, lhs, rest)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def climb(min_bp Int53, lhs Surface, ts Vec(Tok)) PR
+  def climb(min_bp, lhs, [TOp(op) | rest])
+    if lbp(op) >= min_bp do
+      case parse_bp(rbp(op), rest) do
+        PR(rhs, rest2) -> climb(min_bp, SBin(op, lhs, rhs), rest2)
+      end
+    else
+      PR(lhs, [TOp(op) | rest])
+    end
+  end
+  def climb(min_bp, lhs, ts) := PR(lhs, ts)
+
+  def primary(Vec(Tok)) PR
+  def primary([TNum(n) | rest]) := PR(SNum(n), rest)
+  def primary([TId(x) | rest]) := PR(SId(x), rest)
+  def primary([TLP | rest])
+    case parse_bp(0, rest) do
+      PR(e, [TRP | rest2]) -> PR(e, rest2)
+      PR(e, other) -> PR(e, other)
+    end
+  end
+
+  # binding powers (Rian.Pratt's table for the arithmetic slice): `*` > `+`/`-`.
+  def lbp(op String) Int53 := bp_base(level(op))
+  def rbp(op String) Int53 := bp_base(level(op)) + 1
+  def bp_base(lvl Int53) Int53 := (13 - lvl) * 10
+
+  def level(String) Int53
+  def level("*") := 3
+  def level("+") := 4
+  def level("-") := 4
+
+  # ── stage 3: lower (Surface -> Core) ──
+  pub def lower(Surface) Core
+  pub def lower(SNum(t)) := CNum(t)
+  pub def lower(SId(n)) := CId(n)
+  pub def lower(SBin(op, l, r)) := CBin(op, lower(l), lower(r))
+
+  # ── stage 4: forms (Core -> Erlang abstract forms) ──
+  # `String.to_atom` is the one host FFI: Rian cannot spell the operator atoms
+  # (`:+`) or capitalised Erlang variable atoms (`:A`) — counted in @selfhost_ffi.
+  pub def forms(Core) ErlForm
+  pub def forms(CNum(t)) := Integer(1, parse_int(t))
+  pub def forms(CId(n)) := Var(1, String.to_atom(cap(n)))
+  pub def forms(CBin(op, l, r)) := Op(1, String.to_atom(op), forms(l), forms(r))
+
+  def parse_int(s String) Int53 := digits(Prim.str_chars(s), 0)
+  def digits(Vec(Int53), Int53) Int53
+  def digits([], acc) := acc
+  def digits([c | rest], acc) := digits(rest, acc * 10 + c - 48)
+
+  # capitalise the first character (Rian `a` -> Erlang var `A`).
+  def cap(s String) String
+    case Prim.str_chars(s) do
+      [c | rest] -> Prim.str_from_chars([up(c) | rest])
+      [] -> s
+    end
+  end
+
+  def up(c Int53) Int53
+    if c >= 97 and c <= 122 do
+      c - 32
+    else
+      c
+    end
+  end
+end

+defmodule Rian.ComposeFixpointTest do
+  # async: false — loads real modules into the VM via :code.load_binary.
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  alias Rian.Beam
+
+  # COMPOSITION fixpoint (ADR-0063 Step 3): the FIRST genuine composition rung.
+  # `selfhost_compose.rian` wires lex → parse → lower → forms DIRECTLY in Rian over
+  # shared types — `compile(s) = forms(lower(parse(lex(s))))` — with no Elixir glue
+  # between the stages. Its output IS Erlang abstract forms, so this test feeds them
+  # to `:compile.forms`, loads the module, RUNS it, and asserts it behaves
+  # IDENTICALLY to the full Elixir toolchain (`Rian.Beam` compiling the same source).
+  #
+  # This is the difference between per-stage equivalence (every other fixpoint) and
+  # composition: here stage N consumes stage N-1's Rian output with no projection.
+
+  setup_all do
+    {:ok, mod} = Beam.load(File.read!("examples/rian/selfhost_compose.rian"), :rian_compose)
+    {:ok, mod: mod}
+  end
+
+  # build, compile, and load a 0/N-ary `f` whose body is the composed Rian form.
+  defp compose_module(mod, expr, vars, modname) do
+    form = mod.compile(expr)
+    params = Enum.map(vars, fn v -> {:var, 0, var_atom(v)} end)
+    arity = length(vars)
+
+    forms = [
+      {:attribute, 0, :module, modname},
+      {:attribute, 0, :export, [{:f, arity}]},
+      {:function, 0, :f, arity, [{:clause, 0, params, [], [form]}]}
+    ]
+
+    {:ok, ^modname, bin} = :compile.forms(forms, [:return_errors])
+    {:module, ^modname} = :code.load_binary(modname, ~c"nofile", bin)
+    modname
+  end
+
+  # match the pipeline's `cap`: upcase the first char only (`foo` -> `Foo`).
+  defp var_atom(v) do
+    <<c, rest::binary>> = Atom.to_string(v)
+    String.to_atom(String.upcase(<<c>>) <> rest)
+  end
+
+  # the Elixir toolchain compiling the SAME expression as a function body.
+  defp ref_module(expr, vars) do
+    sig = Enum.map_join(vars, ", ", fn v -> "#{v} Int53" end)
+    sig = if sig == "", do: "", else: sig
+    src = "def f(#{sig}) Int53 := #{expr}"
+    {:ok, m} = Beam.load(src, :"cmp_ref_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
+    m
+  end
+
+  # {expr, [free vars], [arg lists to run on both modules]}
+  @corpus [
+    {"a + b", [:a, :b], [[2, 3], [10, -4]]},
+    {"a + b * c", [:a, :b, :c], [[1, 2, 3], [5, 6, 7]]},
+    {"a * b + c", [:a, :b, :c], [[2, 3, 4]]},
+    {"(a + b) * c", [:a, :b, :c], [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]},
+    {"a - b - c", [:a, :b, :c], [[10, 3, 2]]},
+    {"a * (b + c)", [:a, :b, :c], [[2, 3, 4]]},
+    {"x + y * z - w", [:x, :y, :z, :w], [[1, 2, 3, 4]]},
+    {"2 + 3 * 4", [], [[]]},
+    {"foo * bar + 1", [:foo, :bar], [[6, 7]]}
+  ]
+
+  describe "composition fixpoint — lex→parse→lower→forms (Rian) runs identically to Elixir" do
+    test "the composed Rian pipeline compiles + runs a function equal to Rian.Beam's", %{mod: mod} do
+      for {expr, vars, inputs} <- @corpus do
+        composed =
+          compose_module(mod, expr, vars, :"cmp_composed_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
+
+        ref = ref_module(expr, vars)
+
+        for args <- inputs do
+          assert apply(composed, :f, args) == apply(ref, :f, args),
+                 "composed pipeline diverged from Elixir toolchain on `#{expr}` with #{inspect(args)}"
+        end
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "teeth — the stages genuinely COMPOSE (no inter-stage glue)" do
+    test "lex feeds parse feeds lower feeds forms, end to end", %{mod: mod} do
+      # the composed output is a real Erlang abstract form, built only by Rian.
+      assert mod.compile("a + b * 2") ==
+               {:op, 1, :+, {:var, 1, :A}, {:op, 1, :*, {:var, 1, :B}, {:integer, 1, 2}}}
+
+      # and each intermediate is the next stage's input (shared types, no projection)
+      assert mod.lex("a*2") == [{:t_id, "a"}, {:t_op, "*"}, {:t_num, "2"}]
+      assert mod.lower(mod.parse(mod.lex("a*2"))) == {:c_bin, "*", {:c_id, "a"}, {:c_num, "2"}}
+    end
+
+    test "precedence survives the whole pipeline (a + b * c nests * under +)", %{mod: mod} do
+      m = compose_module(mod, "a + b * c", [:a, :b, :c], :cmp_prec)
+      # 2 + 3*4 = 14, not (2+3)*4 = 20 — precedence is preserved through composition
+      assert m.f(2, 3, 4) == 14
+    end
+  end
+end
